title: AuroraCloud x Redwood - Reference Arch + Marketplace Integration Sync
summary: Partner technical sync to align on AuroraCloud marketplace listing, reference architecture diagrams, packaging artifacts (Helm, Terraform), and required security/compliance artifacts. Agreed next steps include draft listing asset handoff, reference arch final review, and a joint demo in a week to validate marketplace provisioning flow.
action_items: Ava Martinez - share Redwood marketplace listing checklist and image assets - due 2026-04-02
Liam O'Connor - confirm marketplace SKU mapping and billing test account - due 2026-04-05
Daniel Kim - produce reference architecture diagram (VPC + Private deploy options) and sample Helm chart - due 2026-04-06
Ethan Zhou - provide required compliance docs (SOC2 scope, encryption policy) and KMS integration notes - due 2026-04-07
next_steps: Redwood to upload draft listing assets to shared drive
AuroraCloud to provision test marketplace account and share credentials (scoped) with Redwood SEs
Schedule joint end-to-end demo for marketplace provisioning and SSO (target 2026-04-08)
Run basic perf smoke test on Dedicated config and share results
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood Partner Eng), Jon Ruiz (Redwood Product), Priya Nair (AuroraCloud PM), Liam O'Connor (AuroraCloud Marketplace Eng), Sofia Reyes (AuroraCloud Solutions Architect), Ethan Zhou (AuroraCloud Security), Clara Gomes (AuroraCloud DevOps)

[00:00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we have about an hour. quick roll call?
[00:00:10] Priya (AuroraCloud): Priya here, thanks Ava.
[00:00:13] Liam (AuroraCloud): Liam here.
[00:00:15] Sofia (AuroraCloud): Sofia here.
[00:00:18] Daniel (Redwood SE): Daniel here.
[00:00:20] Maya (Redwood): Maya here.
[00:00:22] Ethan (AuroraCloud): Ethan - security.
[00:00:24] Clara (AuroraCloud): Clara - DevOps.
[00:00:27] Ava (Redwood): great, ok objective for today, align on the marketplace listing assets and the reference architecture for both hosted and private deployments, plus define the joint solution packaging steps. we put an agenda in the invite but we'll take it in order.

[00:01:12] Ava (Redwood): first on listing - Liam we wanted to confirm Aurora's marketplace metadata fields and required assets. what's the current checklist?
[00:01:25] Liam (AuroraCloud): yeah so, um we need a short description, long description, three marketing images (1280x720 ideally), a 1-2 minute demo video link, pricing SKU info, categories, tags, and a technical artifacts section which can link to a refarch doc and deployment templates. we'll also need test accounts for billing integration, and contact for support.
[00:01:50] Ava (Redwood): perfect — Redwood can provide the descriptions and images, we usually include quickstart, architecture diagram, and a link to our reference deploy repo.
[00:02:03] Priya (AuroraCloud): how does Redwood want to handle the billing model? Aurora's marketplace supports per-hour reserved instances and per-call billing via metered usage; what's Redwood's preferred pattern?
[00:02:18] Jon (Redwood Product): we typically offer both. for marketplace we'd propose a SKU for 'Redwood Hosted' (usage-based per-token) and 'Redwood Dedicated' (monthly reserved). for marketplace integration we can provide a mapped SKU for reserved tiers and a metering callback for hosted. there may be some mapping work.
[00:02:37] Liam (AuroraCloud): ok mapping is fine but we'll need test hooks to validate invoices, so please provide a dev billing account.

[00:03:05] Daniel (Redwood SE): switching to ref arch — we prepared two reference diagrams: one for hosted (Redwood managed in AuroraCloud marketplace region) and one for private/VPC deployment where customer's infra runs Redwood Private with control plane in Aurora. i'm going to share my screen, showing the initial diagram.
[00:03:28] [screen share begins]
[00:03:35] Daniel (Redwood SE): so on the hosted side you can see the marketplace provisioning flow: marketplace -> provisioning lambda -> account on Redwood hosted control plane -> model endpoint in regional GPU pool. there's a note about autoscaling and fallback to smaller quantized variants. some of the auto-transcription here reads 'Redwood Dedicate' instead of 'Dedicated' — apologies if the doc is slightly messy.
[00:04:05] Sofia (AuroraCloud): can you slow for a sec — what's the networking boundary for data in the hosted model? customers want guarantees about data segregation.
[00:04:16] Daniel (Redwood SE): yes good Q. hosted still isolates customer workloads logically; we provide per-tenant namespaces and customer-specific KV cache limits, but data at rest is encrypted using our KMS and for marketplace customers we can offer BYOK on request for enterprise SKUs.
[00:04:33] Ethan (AuroraCloud): BYOK is important, we'll need KMS integration docs and any key rotation policy. also SOC2 scope for logging.
[00:04:45] Maya (Redwood): we have a compliance pack — I'll attach the SOC2 summary and our log retention policy. Redwood logs are audit-trail enabled per tenant.

[00:05:22] Daniel (Redwood SE): now private deployment, diagram shows a small control plane shim in Aurora's region and customer runs inference nodes in their VPC, or in air-gapped mode. deployment options include Helm chart for Kubernetes, and Terraform for cloud infra. Clara, does that align with your infra patterns?
[00:05:38] Clara (AuroraCloud): yes we run EKS and also have a VM-based option. the Helm chart approach is preferred but we need a sample values.yaml and clear resource requests for GPU node pools.
[00:05:50] Daniel (Redwood SE): noted — sample values and recommended node types (A100/80GB or equivalent) will be included. for quantized CPU-based fallbacks we'll document perf expectations.

[00:06:22] Priya (AuroraCloud): quick note — marketplace wants a one-click deploy option if possible, or at least a guided deploy that provisions the infra automatically.
[00:06:35] Ava (Redwood): Redwood supports a one-click pattern via our marketplace provisioning API, we can provide a CloudFormation/Terraform template that the marketplace kicks off. that will live in the technical artifacts area.

[00:07:55] Liam (AuroraCloud): about images — marketing needs transparent screenshots of the console, but we also need to ensure no customer data shows up in screenshots. do you have sanitized console images?
[00:08:10] Maya (Redwood): yes, we have sanitized screenshots and a short video. I'll hand off the high-res assets.

[00:08:50] Ethan (AuroraCloud): security items — SSO/SAML support, RBAC mapping from Aurora marketplace identity to Redwood roles, and audit logs. can you describe SSO flow for the joint solution?
[00:09:05] Daniel (Redwood SE): sure — the marketplace can act as the identity provider for initial provisioning; we support SAML and OIDC. after provisioning customers can SSO into Redwood Console via SAML with group-to-role mapping. we'll document attribute mapping. expect a small mapping table: email/name/teams -> RBAC role.
[00:09:25] Ethan (AuroraCloud): perfect. also, any inbound ports for private deployment? we prefer no public inbound — all control plane communication should be egress-only unless customer explicitly opens a management endpoint.
[00:09:37] Daniel (Redwood SE): we support an egress-only model via agent plus websocket tunnel; we'll include both patterns in the ref arch doc.

[00:10:12] Sofia (AuroraCloud): on joint solution packaging — we'd like a ready repo with Helm charts and Terraform module. can Redwood add examples for typical patterns: small dev (1 GPU), medium (2-4 GPUs), production (autoscale pools)?
[00:10:28] Daniel (Redwood SE): yes, sample overlays for dev/staging/prod with resource profiles will be provided. we'll add knobs for quantization profiles and KV cache sizes.

[00:11:05] Priya (AuroraCloud): timeline — marketplace listing needs to be approved by Aurora's cert team; that process takes 5-7 business days once assets are submitted. can we aim to have initial assets by 2026-04-02?
[00:11:19] Ava (Redwood): yes we can target that. action: we'll upload draft assets on 4/2.

[00:11:40] [long section discussing test flows and demo setup]
[00:11:45] Liam (AuroraCloud): for billing test hooks we'll need a webhook or reporting endpoint from Redwood to validate metered usage. does Redwood have a sandbox metering API?
[00:12:00] Jon (Redwood Product): we do. we'll provide sandbox endpoints and sample payloads. for reserved SKUs we can do a monthly invoice simulation.

[00:12:30] Daniel (Redwood SE): performance note — if you run a Dedicated GPU pool with 8xA100s you'll see sub-30ms token latencies on our optimized LM configs for shorter seqs; quantized variants trade off quality for cost and are good for burst/low-cost tiers. We'll add perf numbers to the ref arch doc.
[00:12:55] Sofia (AuroraCloud): can you call out memory requirements for the models? we need that for node autoscaler config.
[00:13:05] Daniel (Redwood SE): yes approximate per-model footprints will be included. small models ~8-16GB, medium ~24-40GB, large >80GB depending on variants.

[00:13:30] [transcription glitch - 'kv cash' instead of 'KV cache']

[00:13:40] Ava (Redwood): thanks — moving to E2E testing and certification. Aurora's cert team will want test cases: provisioning flow, SSO, billing, deploy, scale, and failover tests. we'll coordinate a test plan doc.
[00:13:55] Priya (AuroraCloud): yes we'll send our cert checklist after this.

[00:14:30] Maya (Redwood): on the joint solution marketing side, do you want Redwood to co-brand in the listing? we usually do co-branded logos for partners.
[00:14:40] Priya (AuroraCloud): yes co-brand is good. marketing alignment can happen separately but we can start with assets.

[00:15:05] [longer technical Q&A about upgrades and rollbacks]
[00:15:12] Daniel (Redwood SE): upgrades for private deploy are handled via Helm bump and job-based canary - we support A/B rollouts with automatic fallback. we'll document rollback steps.
[00:15:33] Clara (AuroraCloud): do you expose health endpoints for the orchestrator so our monitoring can scrape?
[00:15:40] Daniel (Redwood SE): yes prometheus metrics and healthz endpoints included. sample grafana dashboard will be in the repo.

[00:16:10] [discussion about support model]
[00:16:18] Ava (Redwood AE): support model — for marketplace customers we propose triaged support: Aurora handles first-line, Redwood does second-line. we'll provide runbook docs and support contact.
[00:16:32] Priya (AuroraCloud): that works. we'll add the support contact fields in the listing metadata.

[00:17:05] [noise / brief audio glitch]

[00:17:20] Ethan (AuroraCloud): on compliance: please share SOC2 report redacted and any penetration test summaries. we'll need to store them in our partner vault.
[00:17:33] Maya (Redwood): yes, I'll share the SOC2 summary and PT overview.

[00:18:05] [mid-call recap]

[00:18:10] Ava (Redwood): quick recap — Redwood to share listing assets + screenshots + video by 4/2; Daniel to share ref arch diagram + Helm/Terraform samples by 4/6; Aurora to provide test billing account and cert checklist by 4/5; security docs shared by Redwood by 4/7. plan a joint demo 4/8 to run through provisioning path.

[00:19:00] [deeper technical dive led by Daniel]

[00:19:10] Daniel (Redwood SE): showing sample Helm values now. note: GPU autoscaling is handled external to the chart, but we provide recommended HPA/Taints and tolerations. also the runtime supports continuous batching and an option to enable KV cache persistence to reduce cold-start token costs.
[00:19:45] Sofia (AuroraCloud): how do you manage model updates — is there a model registry?
[00:19:53] Daniel (Redwood SE): yes we have a model catalog and version pinning; marketplace can surface the default pinned version but customers can opt to upgrade or pin. rollout policies support canary, A/B, and automatic rollback on error rate.

[00:20:20] [some crosstalk, 'uhh' 'right' in background]

[00:21:05] Priya (AuroraCloud): about joint solution naming in the marketplace — any naming conventions?
[00:21:12] Ava (Redwood): we usually do 'Redwood Inference - <Partner>' or 'Redwood on AuroraCloud'. we'll send a naming suggestion list.

[00:22:00] Liam (AuroraCloud): one nit — the marketplace security review needs network diagrams showing ports and flow; Daniel please include a simplified L3/L4 diagram for cert.
[00:22:15] Daniel (Redwood SE): will do.

[00:23:00] [timeouts: brief silence as files are located]

[00:24:05] Clara (AuroraCloud): for private deploys, do you support air-gapped image bundles for customers that cannot reach external registries?
[00:24:15] Daniel (Redwood SE): yes we can provide tarball images and an offline installer; we'll add an air-gap checklist with required network policies and file hashes.

[00:25:20] [discussion about telemetry and PII]
[00:25:30] Ethan (AuroraCloud): telemetry: we need to ensure no PII is sent to Redwood logs by default. is there a redaction option?
[00:25:40] Maya (Redwood): yes redaction toggles exist and we document default retention and opt-out steps.

[00:26:05] Ava (Redwood): ok timecheck — about 30 minutes left, i want to make sure we covered the marketplace provisioning E2E. Daniel, can you run us through the typical provisioning sequence?
[00:26:18] Daniel (Redwood SE): sure — marketplace order triggers provisioning lambda -> calls Redwood provisioning API with marketplace metadata -> Redwood creates tenant + provision endpoints in regional pool -> if private option selected the marketplace triggers terraform module to provision infra in customer account and seat licensing; SSO metadata is exchanged and onboarding email goes out.
[00:26:50] Priya (AuroraCloud): is there a webhook we can use to surface provisioning status in Aurora's console?
[00:26:58] Daniel (Redwood SE): yes we emit lifecycle webhooks and status endpoints. we'll include sample webhook payloads.

[00:27:40] [short break in transcript while people review diagrams]

[00:28:10] Liam (AuroraCloud): another ask — marketplace approval requires a security contact and SLA summary. do you have a standard SLA we can include?
[00:28:22] Ava (Redwood): yes we have an SLA template for hosted and for Dedicated/reserved customers. we'll include basic uptime guarantees and escalation contacts.

[00:29:00] Daniel (Redwood SE): technical tangent — caching: our KV cache can be pinned to regional redis, we recommend sticky sessions for low-latency workloads. if using private deploy, the cache can be deployed in the customer's VPC.

[00:29:40] Sofia (AuroraCloud): for observability we need traces for request-level tracking; does Redwood have tracing integrations?
[00:29:50] Daniel (Redwood SE): yes we support OpenTelemetry and can export traces to a customer collector or send to Redwood observability for partners with consent.

[00:30:15] [transcription shows 'quantise' instead of 'quantize']

[00:30:40] Ava (Redwood): let's capture decisions — documented in action items.

[00:31:00] [deep technical Q&A continues covering node sizing, cost estimates, and sample benchmarks]

[00:38:40] Daniel (Redwood SE): just shared a slide with benchmark numbers — 99th p90 latencies, throughput for batching. note that perf is very workload dependent so we recommend a short benchmark POC for your expected prompt distribution.
[00:39:10] Priya (AuroraCloud): we'll coordinate a POC window.

[00:40:00] [discussion about legal/contract triggers for Dedicated offering]

[00:41:05] Jon (Redwood Product): for Dedicated reserved capacity we'll need an MSA or addendum; sales will follow up but for marketplace listing it's fine to show pricing tiers and 'contact for enterprise' CTA.

[00:42:20] Priya (AuroraCloud): ok marketing question — can Redwood provide customer success stories or a short case study for the listing?
[00:42:30] Ava (Redwood): we have a short anonymized case study we can include.

[00:43:00] [wrap-up planning]

[00:43:12] Ava (Redwood): last thing - demo scheduling. is 2026-04-08 good for everyone?
[00:43:20] Priya (AuroraCloud): yes that works.
[00:43:22] Liam (AuroraCloud): ok.
[00:43:25] Sofia (AuroraCloud): yes.

[00:43:40] Ava (Redwood): excellent. any final questions?
[00:43:50] Ethan (AuroraCloud): just one — for the BYOK flow, do you support importing customer keys into Redwood KMS or do you connect to customer KMS?
[00:44:02] Daniel (Redwood SE): we support both patterns: integrate with customer KMS (via IAM role) for hosted enterprise SKUs, or accept a wrapped key for BYOK. docs will include steps.

[00:44:25] Priya (AuroraCloud): great. if nothing else we'll call it. thanks all.

[00:44:35] Ava (Redwood): thanks — we'll send the notes and action items.

[00:44:50] [post-meeting small talk and ends]

Recap / Next steps repeated: Redwood to deliver listing assets (screenshots, descriptions, video), ref arch + Helm/Terraform samples, perf notes, and security docs. Aurora to provide cert checklist, test billing account, and schedule demo.

End of transcript.
